paragraphs.en: Players take turns accumulating rolls towards 21. In Two dice, use both below 16 and one die from 16. In One die, use one throughout. After the first roll you may stand. Reaching 21 or exceeding it ends your turn.

Finish every player’s turn before scoring. A unique best total not exceeding 21 earns one point, or two for exactly 21. A tied best total, including tied 21s, and an all-bust round earn no points. This match scoring also applies to the one-die variant; it replaces a playoff. Rotate the first player each round. First to the chosen target (default ten) wins.

Each round starts with an automatic opening contribution from every active player: ten chips by default, or the table setting. A player with less pays their entire balance and is all-in. Then players act in seat order: check if nothing is owed, call a raise, raise, fold, or go all-in. A raise makes the others respond again. Betting closes when all players who still have chips have responded and matched the current bet, or only one player has not folded. All-in players keep their right to play without further betting. A short all-in does not reopen raising for someone who already acted unless the cumulative increase reaches a full raise.

Use C to check or call, F to fold, A for all-in, and R or B to type your own raise. The entered amount is the increase above the current bet; any amount needed to call is added to the payment. Raises start at one chip and later must match the last full raise; a smaller final all-in is allowed. Preset raises are also in the actions list. Cards or dice start only after betting closes.

Before any dice, use Virtual chips under Round settlement to play with opening contributions and betting. Set initial chips, opening contribution and round limit when creating the table. Defaults are 100 chips, an opening contribution of ten and ten rounds. Point mode retains its scoring without chip betting.

After betting, players who have not folded take their dice turns, including all-in players. Contributions create main and side pots: a player may win only the layers their own contribution covers. Each layer goes to its highest non-bust eligible total; tied leaders split it, with remaining whole chips assigned in round seat order. An unmatched excess is returned. A layer with no eligible non-bust total is refunded to its contributors. If everyone but one folds, the remaining player wins the contested pot without rolling. Chips in balances and pots are conserved.

The starting seat rotates each round. A zero balance eliminates only after settlement. Play ends at the round limit or with fewer than two funded players. The highest final balance wins; tied maxima draw. S reads balances. Previously recorded chip games retain their original betting rules.

Use the arrows to choose an action and Enter to perform it. Tab changes fields. T reads the current turn; S reads scores. F1 opens the current shortcut reference; Ctrl+F1 opens the rules. Card hands preserve physical card identity and draw order. Their cards are for inspection, not play: choose decisions in the separate actions list.
